prs.title: fix(usePress): only skip Enter default prevention on macOS for Control + Enter
prs.author: jsabutis
prs.body:
Closes #10741

On macOS, `shouldPreventDefaultKeyboard` returned `false` for every Enter keypress. The #10237 exemption for Control + Enter (native context menu) only checked the key, so plain Enter stopped being default-prevented too. When a press handler moves focus during keydown, as a Select option does when it restores focus to its trigger, the browser fires its native click on the newly focused trigger and the Select reopens.

This passes the event to `shouldPreventDefaultKeyboard` and requires `ctrlKey` for the exemption. Control + Enter keeps its default, so the `contextmenu` path is unchanged. Plain Enter falls through to the existing rules, so links, submit buttons and inputs keep their native Enter behaviour.

prs.title: fix: scroll anchoring improvements for chat
prs.author: yihuiliao
prs.body:
This PR fixes a couple of things. Some of which were from testing in July and some that were noticed while making the ai component docs.

1) Updates the width of the Chat in storybook so it fits on mobile screens
2) Removes unneeded state to calculate scroll anchoring (see devon's [comment](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10258#discussion_r3659717895))
3) Fixes the scroll positioning from jumping on mobile
4) Expanding and collapsing response status in virtualized chat thread has weird scroll behavior (like it is opening upward).

For 2, I removed the `hadEstimatedVisibleItems` / `wasNearAnchorEdge` fields that tried to remember whether we were near the bottom while estimated items were measuring and used that to skip preserving the item anchor on later passes. Now, we check proximity before each layout pass. Separately, we check whether the resize batch includes the newest content. If only older items resized, we preserve the reading position instead of snapping to the bottom just because we’re within the threshold.

For 3, scroll position jumped on mobile, an item can only be anchored if it fits fully inside the viewport. On mobile, one tall item can fill the whole screen, so nothing ever fully fit and no anchor was picked. Now we anchor to the item closest to the edge even if it's partly cut off, falling back to the least-cut-off item if none fit.
